dingo.name: dingo
dingo.summary: A lineage of wild dog found in Australia, closely related to the New Guinea singing dog, with the oldest known Australian remains about 3,500 years old.

pama-nyungan-languages.name: Pama–Nyungan languages
pama-nyungan-languages.summary: The largest family of Australian Aboriginal languages, comprising most of the continent's roughly 400 Aboriginal languages, identified and named by linguist Kenneth L. Hale.

max-planck-institute-for-evolutionary-an.name: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology
max-planck-institute-for-evolutionary-an.summary: A research institute in Leipzig, Germany, founded in 1997, central to the development of archaeogenetics and molecular anthropology as scientific fields.
max-planck-institute-for-evolutionary-an.source_title: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology

haplogroup-c-m130.name: Haplogroup C*
haplogroup-c-m130.summary: The base branch of Y-chromosome Haplogroup C, found in ancient populations on every continent except Africa and dominant among many indigenous peoples of East Asia, Siberia, North America and Australia.

wandjina.name: Wandjina
wandjina.summary: Cloud and rain spirit beings of the Wanjina Wunggurr Aboriginal peoples of the Kimberley region, depicted in rock art dating back roughly 4,000 years and still culturally significant today.

kimberley-western-australia.name: The Kimberley
kimberley-western-australia.summary: The northernmost of Western Australia's nine regions, bordered by the Indian Ocean and the Timor Sea, named in 1879 after the Earl of Kimberley.

rainbow-serpent.name: Rainbow Serpent
rainbow-serpent.summary: A creator deity common across Aboriginal Australian traditions, associated with water; it gives life but can bring chaos when disturbed.

gwion-gwion-rock-paintings.name: Gwion Gwion rock paintings
gwion-gwion-rock-paintings.summary: A tradition of ancient rock art in the Kimberley region of Western Australia depicting human figures, with most works estimated to be about 12,000 years old.

university-of-western-australia.name: University of Western Australia
university-of-western-australia.summary: Public research university in Crawley, Western Australia, established in 1911, and one of Australia's 'sandstone universities' as well as a member of the Group of Eight.
